fichas.title: Drive-in cinemas
fichas.summary: Drive-in cinema layouts use curved, sloping ramps to raise the front of cars and maintain rear-seat sightlines to the screen. The page describes site access, ticketing, screen placement and construction, projection facilities, in-car sound, heating, and supporting amenities. A fan-shaped layout and a double-screen arrangement are illustrated.
uses: Screen films to audiences seated in cars
Provide vehicle access, ticket checking, and circulation
Provide sound and optional heating to parked cars

Entrance road: with waiting area, in order to
avoid backing up of traffic on the road. Drivepast ticket counter, so that tickets from the
cars can be checked ---> 0.
Exit: ideally after leaving the ramp forwards.
Detailing of the entire area to avoid dust and
skidding in wet weather.

f) Ramp arrangement and dimensions: elevations can be different according to screen picture height

Ticket counter: one counter for 300 cars;
two for 600; three for 800; four for 1000.
Screen: depends on the number of cars: for
650 cars 14.50 x 11.30 m; for 950 cars 17.0
x 13.0 m. Ideally facing east or north, which
enables earlier performances. For the Central
European latitude, the screen is better
installed in a solid, permanent structure.

Cinema screen in the Billbrook drive-in
cinema near Hamburg: 36 m high x 15.5 m
wide. Height above ground level depends
on ramp gradient and sight angle. Screen
tilted upward avoids distortion. Scaffolding
and screen must be able to bear wind
loading.
Rows of seats should be provided, and a
play area for children is also a good idea.
;
0

Projection building: mostly central, at a
distance of 100 m from the screen.
Projection room contains projectors,
generators, sound amplification system.

entrance

f) Double cinema. One projection room for both screens, with the possibility of staggered starting times. All
other areas (cash desks, bar, toilets etc.) are common

226

Sound reproduction ideally has loudspeakers
inside the cars; the loudspeakers are
attached to a post for every two cars at 5.0
m separation and are attached inside the cars
by the visitors.
Heating: on loudspeaker posts, possibly
also a connection for heating in the cars.

fichas.title: Double drive-in cinema
fichas.summary: The illustrated double cinema serves two screens from one projection room, allowing staggered starting times. Shared facilities include cash desks, a bar, and toilets; the plan also shows separate projection surfaces, car ramps, waiting areas, and a central entrance and ticket office.
uses: Show films on two screens, with the option of staggered starting times
Share support facilities between both cinema areas
figure_refs: 3 Double cinema. One projection room for both screens, with the possibility of staggered starting times. All other areas (cash desks, bar, toilets etc.) are common
